scope: Primary-source refresh for German-first local realtime voice. Source evidence only; no target-runtime, German E2E, Trigger4, or acceptance credit.

observed: FastTurn combines acoustic cues with streaming CTC-derived semantic cues for low-latency turn detection.
Its released evaluation material explicitly includes overlap, backchannels, pauses, pitch variation and environmental noise.
findings.project_delta: Promote FastTurn from generic literature reference to a high-value T7-TURN-001 discriminator/dataset-method donor for Frankenstein false-endpoint, overlap, backchannel and interruption tests.
findings.negative_space: No German-specific endpoint quality, target-host latency, cancellation correctness, or Frankenstein ABI integration was observed here.

observed: Official Qwen3-TTS exposes 0.6B/1.7B models, Apache-2.0 source, German support, streaming speech generation, voice design and voice cloning.
Current package metadata and issue traffic show nontrivial runtime/streaming dependency and compatibility risk.
findings.project_delta: Keep Qwen3-TTS first in the expressive German TTS benchmark order, but gate streaming credit on target-host TTFA/RTF/cancellation reproduction. Piper/Thorsten remains the tiny deterministic latency floor.
findings.negative_space: No local target-host execution, male identity stability, ExpressionVector control, German pronunciation score, TTFA, RTF or long-session evidence was observed in this run.

observed: German Thorsten Piper ONNX artifacts remain available under MIT metadata; the high model is approximately 114 MB and has a published SHA-256.
findings.project_delta: Retain Piper/Thorsten as the low-footprint deterministic German TTS latency/resource floor for the same host and sentence corpus used by expressive challengers.
findings.negative_space: No claim that Piper matches the desired conversational naturalness or state-driven expressive control.

observed: Qwen3-ASR-0.6B remains an Apache-2.0 multilingual ASR candidate with explicit German support; the current model tree reports a roughly 1.88 GB safetensors artifact.
findings.project_delta: No ranking promotion beyond existing T7-ASR-001. The decisive test remains identical real German room audio against donor Whisper and Nemotron 3.5 Streaming under measured endpoint/partial-transcript latency.
findings.negative_space: No target-host WER/CER/latency evidence in this run.

observed: Parallel Trigger-7 work pinned Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B at revision 851bf6e806efd8d0a36b00ddf55e13ccb7b8cd0a.
SandLogicTechnologies/Qwen3.5-4B-GGUF Q4_K_M is pinned at revision 5520227b6782610f3e8e080edd1867558d3856f1 with reported SHA-256 f987bfd0fccb9bfb76e0926eb05f34ba96401f901b0204b7043608488f4f7422.
findings.project_delta: The official-family Q4 control is no longer a source-pinning blocker. The next gate is clay-direct-dev quarantine download, recomputed hash, load identity and German baseline-vs-abliterated A/B.
findings.negative_space: The community Q4 has not been target-downloaded, hash-verified or executed; benchmark/runtime credit remains zero.

hypothesis_update: Lane A remains favored. The strongest near-term improvement is tighter causal turn control: streaming ASR plus acoustic-semantic endpoint intelligence feeding cancellation-safe local inference and expressive streaming TTS.
counterhypothesis: FastTurn-like semantic endpointing may add model/ASR latency and complexity without improving German Frankenstein turn behavior enough to beat tuned acoustic VAD plus a simpler endpoint heuristic.
cheapest_high_information_discriminator: After the already-dispatched hardware roundtrip reaches a terminal executable state, replay a pinned German pause/backchannel/overlap corpus on clay-direct-dev through donor endpointing versus a FastTurn-derived or equivalent acoustic-semantic controller while holding audio transport and ASR fixed; compare false endpoints, late endpoints and barge-in cancellation latency.
